[Design System] This project uses the **picsee — Quiet Image Canvas primitives** design system. This is a binding choice for visual style — every visual must follow it. Don't invent colors, type, spacing, or components not grounded here.

Scope: the design system is a visual style reference only. Its guide may describe example products, brands, or people unrelated to the user and to the subject of this conversation. Never treat anything in the design system as a fact about the user, their work, or the topic.

**Loading the bundle is how you use this design system.** Every page you build must load `_ds/picsee-ui-system/_ds_bundle.js` and compose with the components it exports on `window.PicseeUiSystem_bb8eab` — do not recreate those components from scratch or restyle raw HTML to look like them. The bundle calls `React.createElement`, so `window.React` and `window.ReactDOM` must load first — the pinned tags below provide them. Add these once:

```html
<!-- React first — the bundle calls React.createElement -->
<script src="https://unpkg.com/react@18.3.1/umd/react.development.js" integrity="sha384-hD6/rw4ppMLGNu3tX5cjIb+uRZ7UkRJ6BPkLpg4hAu/6onKUg4lLsHAs9EBPT82L" crossorigin="anonymous"></script>
<script src="https://unpkg.com/react-dom@18.3.1/umd/react-dom.development.js" integrity="sha384-u6aeetuaXnQ38mYT8rp6sbXaQe3NL9t+IBXmnYxwkUI2Hw4bsp2Wvmx4yRQF1uAm" crossorigin="anonymous"></script>
<link rel="stylesheet" href="_ds/picsee-ui-system/tokens/globals.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="_ds/picsee-ui-system/tokens/light.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="_ds/picsee-ui-system/tokens/dark.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="_ds/picsee-ui-system/components/primitives.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="_ds/picsee-ui-system/styles.css">
<script src="_ds/picsee-ui-system/_ds_bundle.js"></script>
```

With several design systems bound, keep each system's stylesheets together and load the PRIMARY system's `<link>`s LAST so its tokens win.

The bundle is plain compiled JS — load it with a regular `<script>` (no `type="text/babel"` or `type="module"`). Every component is then available on `window.PicseeUiSystem_bb8eab` — e.g. `const { IconButton, Keycap } = window.PicseeUiSystem_bb8eab;`. The linked stylesheet(s) carry the design tokens (colors, type, spacing) — style against those via `var(--*)` and the design system's classes rather than guessing values.

Your own page code stays separate from the bundle: write it in `<script type="text/babel">` blocks, with Babel standalone loaded once (pinned tag below) to transpile your JSX in the browser —

```html
<script src="https://unpkg.com/@babel/standalone@7.29.0/babel.min.js" integrity="sha384-m08KidiNqLdpJqLq95G/LEi8Qvjl/xUYll3QILypMoQ65QorJ9Lvtp2RXYGBFj1y" crossorigin="anonymous"></script>
<script type="text/babel">
  const { IconButton, Keycap } = window.PicseeUiSystem_bb8eab;
  ReactDOM.createRoot(document.getElementById('root')).render(<IconButton />);
</script>
```

In text/babel blocks, never give a top-level binding a window-global name — `status`, `name`, `open`, `close`, `top`, `self`, `parent`, `origin`, `event`, `length`, `location`, `history`, `screen`, `scroll`, `stop`, `print`, `focus`, `blur`, `frames`, `closed`, `opener`. Babel injects the transpiled code as a classic script (top-level const/let become var), so `const status = …` writes `window.status`, which coerces or misbehaves, and the page dies with an error the console may never show. Use a longer name (`statusBadge`, `openItems`).

Everything beyond this runtime copy — mocks to fork, specimens, ui_kits, component source — lives in the design system's source tree at `design/picsee-ui-system/`; read from there for anything not under `_ds/picsee-ui-system/`. Its guide is reproduced below so you don't need to fetch it:

<design-system-guide>
# picsee — Quiet Image Canvas primitives

Binding visual guide: `design/DESIGN.md` (relative to the project root). This system serves the accepted C layout for a native macOS local image viewer; browser prototypes are design aids, not native implementation.

Use cool neutral surfaces, one blue accent, flat navigation rows, 12/13/14/16px system typography, 4/6/10px radii, fine dividers and one restrained popover shadow. Images are content, not decorative cards. Grid mode has a compact native title strip and bottom tools. Viewer mode has no application top toolbar; controls appear on demand. Filmstrip integrates paging instead of duplicating it. Keep keyboard focus distinct from selection, and remove hidden tools from interaction and accessibility trees.

Load the compiled bundle and compose IconButton, Keycap and NavRow. Theme classes live on HTML. Use the tokens in tokens/globals.css, light.css and dark.css; do not invent per-screen colors. Actual hit targets, focus handling, contrast and screen-reader behavior require implementation checks; a visual artifact does not certify accessibility.

The palette and primitive token values originated in mdpro commit cee9af46f390b82f3df656552fe7e46da8870ddd. That is provenance only. Markdown editor layouts, Tauri assumptions, upstream ADRs and contrast exceptions do not apply. Some unused token names remain for compatibility with existing exports; they do not introduce editor features. Original visual source and cleanup are documented in design/IMPORT.md.

## Native implementation specifications

Native work must first read the source documents below (paths relative to the project root). Consumed `_ds/` runtime copies contain the Web bundle and visual guide; native specifications remain in the source system.

- `design/picsee-ui-system/native/README.md`: entry point and scope.
- `design/picsee-ui-system/native/TOKEN_MAPPING.md` and `TOKEN_REGISTRY.json`: semantic role whitelist, theme expressions, unit conversion and source hashes.
- `design/picsee-ui-system/native/COMPONENT_CONTRACTS.md`: proposed native component inputs, states, responsibility and acceptance.
- `design/picsee-ui-system/native/NATIVE_MAPPING.md`: SwiftUI/AppKit ownership, appearance/focus/backing conversion and P0-08 handoff.

Web prototypes continue to use the compiled React primitives. Native implementation consumes these contracts and native resource adapters, not the React bundle. PicseeDesignKit is a logical grouping inside existing UI targets, not another production target. UI primitives do not own decoder/cache/file permissions, selection reducers or hide timers. Native APIs and accessibility behavior require SDK compilation and Mac verification before being claimed complete.
</design-system-guide>

Per-component usage notes follow — the first lines of each component's `*.prompt.md`. These are NOT bound into `_ds/picsee-ui-system/`, so they're reproduced here (full files live in the source tree above):

<ds-prompt-excerpts>
### components/IconButton.prompt.md
Use for compact toolbar actions with an accessible name and a single outline icon.

`<IconButton label="切换侧栏" onClick={toggle}><Icon /></IconButton>`

Use pressed for toggles, disabled for unavailable navigation. All styles derive from the imported mdpro tokens.

### components/Keycap.prompt.md
Show a real keyboard shortcut as a compact monospace keycap.

`<Keycap>Space</Keycap>`

This is an explanatory label, not a clickable control.

### components/NavRow.prompt.md
Use a flat sidebar row for folders and library views, with accent-soft selection.

`<NavRow label="日本 · 山海之间" count={12} selected onClick={selectFolder} />`

The optional icon inherits currentColor. No resting card border or shadow.
</ds-prompt-excerpts>

Prop contracts per component (from each `.d.ts`). Prop names are exhaustive — do not invent props. Enum props list every allowed value; `*` marks the default. Never pass a value outside these lists:

<ds-component-props>
IconButton — label: string · children: React.ReactNode · onClick: function · pressed: boolean · disabled: boolean
Keycap — children: React.ReactNode
NavRow — label: string · icon: React.ReactNode · count: number · selected: boolean · onClick: function
</ds-component-props>
